answer_text: Der Spiegel reports a hacker attack on SAP's GitHub accounts. SAP confirms suspicious activity on its GitHub platform but has not called it an attack in its own words, and says it has no sign customers' data was reached.
label: Reported

question_text: Was SAP customer data taken in the GitHub incident?
answer_text: SAP says it has found no sign so far that anyone got into its customers' business data. That is the company's word; nobody outside has checked it.
label: Reported

question_text: Which organisations use SAP, and were they affected?
answer_text: SAP is best known for business software that organisations use to run finance, HR and sales. No organisation has said publicly that it was affected, and SAP says it has no sign customers' data was reached.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: An organisation, SAP or a regulator saying a customer was affected.

question_text: Was SAP's source code stolen or changed?
answer_text: Not established. An insider cited by Der Spiegel says attackers copied and changed SAP code on GitHub using stolen staff tokens. SAP has not said what was accessed.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: SAP saying which code or repositories were reached, whether anything was changed, and whether any changed code reached customers.

question_text: Did the attackers use AI in the SAP incident?
answer_text: Not established. Der Spiegel reports the attackers may have had help from AI systems. Nobody has said what the AI did, and SAP has not commented.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: SAP or investigators describing how the attack was carried out.

question_text: Who is behind the SAP incident, and how did they get in?
what_would_settle_it: SAP, investigators or an independent analysis naming who was responsible and how the staff tokens were obtained.
